title: 569. Perfect Number

examples.explanation: Its proper divisors 1, 2, 4, 7 and 14 add up to 28.
The proper divisors 1, 2 and 4 sum to 7, not 8.
1 has no proper divisors, so the empty sum 0 differs from 1.

hints: Only trial divisors up to the square root are needed; each divisor d pairs with num / d.
Start the total at 1 for num > 1 and take care not to double-count a square root.
